Walichu Caves lie beside Lake Argentino in the surroundings of El Calafate. Rock shelters and lakeside cliffs preserve traces of Patagonia's ancient inhabitants. Here, the history of human settlement unfolds against a backdrop of open steppe, pale stone, and the waters of a vast glacial lake.

The Punta Walichu archaeological route introduces visitors to the region's rock art. During a visit, you can see ancient images and reproductions of drawings that help tell the story of the cultures of the area's earlier inhabitants. The walk combines archaeological discoveries with views of Lake Argentino; excursions from El Calafate may also pair it with a drive along the lakeshore.

At Weg naar Zee, your eyes are immediately drawn to flashes of red against the water and dark mud. At low tide, birds feed on exposed mudflats, mangroves line the shore, and a broad Atlantic sky stretches above them. When scarlet ibises take flight, the flock becomes the highlight of the walk for a few unforgettable seconds.

The name Weg naar Zee means "road to the sea." From the outskirts of Paramaribo, the route passes through open wetlands toward the coast. It is a fascinating place to watch shorebirds and see how the tide changes their feeding grounds. Time of day, season, and water level all matter here.

On Ada Tours birdwatching itineraries, Weg naar Zee is visited after a morning outing to Noordwijkweg. The main purpose of this part of the day is to observe scarlet ibises, and the guide selects observation points according to the birds' current activity. This is a rewarding stop for travelers who want to experience Suriname's wildlife beyond forest trails and encounter nature on the ocean shore.

Whalers Bay lies on Deception Island within a flooded volcanic caldera. A gently sloping beach of dark ash extends along the water. Beyond it rise volcanic slopes and the remains of buildings from an old whaling station.

Rusted tanks and other remnants of the industry recall a time when this natural harbor welcomed whaling vessels. Seabirds can be found around the bay. A landing allows visitors to explore the volcanic shore and view the historic structures from permitted areas.
